name: Flint River Outpost
unique: Canoe and kayak rentals on the Flint from a riverside campground, with a shuttle and a long run that starts at the Radium Springs landing and takes you past limestone bluffs and sandbars.
buzz: The eight mile run is the standard and takes about three hours at a drift. Bring water, there is almost no shade on the gravel bars in July.

name: Camilla Depot Art Gallery
customer: Art browsers, rail fans, road trippers
unique: A restored early 1900s railroad depot at Broad and 19 that serves as the town welcome center and hangs local artists on the old freight walls.
buzz: Small, free and staffed by someone who knows the county. Good place to ask where the good produce stand is.

name: Stripling Irrigation Research Park
unique: A University of Georgia irrigation research facility with variable rate pivot systems and soil moisture instrumentation in working fields, the engineering behind how the southeast waters a crop.
buzz: Not a tourist site and better for it. Arrange a visit if you farm, study water or just want to see how a pivot is tested.

name: Seminole State Park
unique: A campground on the bank of Lake Seminole under big hardwoods, with a swimming beach and a boat ramp a hundred yards from the tent pads, and alligators in the shallows.
buzz: People camp here to fish at daylight, and the lakeside sites are the ones to ask for. Quiet, cheap and full of birds.

name: Lake Seminole
dates: Year round, best spring and autumn
unique: Thirty seven thousand acres where the Flint and Chattahoochee meet to form the Apalachicola, with standing timber in the shallows and a bass fishery ranked among the best in the country.
buzz: Anglers rate it top five nationally for largemouth. The standing timber eats lower units, so idle through the stumps the first time out.

name: Cummings Landing
unique: A county boat landing on Lake Seminole with a ramp, a dock and a picnic shade, the kind of free public water access that makes this lake usable without a marina membership.
buzz: Locals launch here for catfish and crappie and stay for the sunset over the water. No facilities beyond the basics.

name: Earle May Boat Basin Park
unique: A city park on the Flint River with a boat basin, a campground and a fishing pier, the launch point for a river the legislature named the Bass Capital of Georgia.
buzz: Tournament anglers launch before light and the park fills with trailers. The pier is good for people without a boat.

name: Bainbridge Historic District
unique: A courthouse square laid out around Willis Park with a 1902 courthouse, live oaks and a commercial block that steps down to the Flint River bluff.
buzz: The square and the bluff street below it are both walkable in an hour. Best light is late afternoon under the oaks.

name: Bainbridge Little Theatre
unique: A community theatre that has been running a full season of comedies, dramas and musicals for decades in a converted building downtown, with local casts and a real set shop.
buzz: Tickets are cheap and the room sells out for the big musicals. The volunteers run the bar at intermission.

name: Jackie Robinson Birthplace Marker
company: City of Cairo / Georgia Historical Society
unique: A marker on the Cairo street where Jackie Robinson was born in 1919, in a town that was a cotton and peanut market before it was anything else.
buzz: A ten minute stop that lands harder than expected once you read the date and the county. Pair it with the downtown square.

name: Zebulon Theater
unique: A small town movie house still showing first run films under a vertical neon blade sign on Broad Street, with live shows mixed into the calendar.
buzz: Popcorn prices from another decade and a room that has not been multiplexed. It is the evening plan in Cairo.

name: Wolf Creek Trout Lily Preserve
dates: Late February to mid March, then closed for the year
unique: A hardwood slope above a creek that blooms into the largest known stand of trout lilies in the world, millions of them, for about three weeks each February.
buzz: The bloom window is short and people drive from across the state. Walk the boardwalk, stay off the slope, and check the volunteer hotline before coming.

name: Grady County Museum
unique: A county collection covering the turpentine camps, the syrup industry and the railroad that made Cairo a market town, with photographs of a downtown that has lost most of its buildings.
buzz: Volunteer run with limited hours. The syrup and cane grinding material is the part worth asking about.

name: Calvary Mule Day
unique: A small community north of Cairo that closes for a day of mule pulling, cane grinding, syrup boiling and plate lunches, the working end of south Georgia farm life rather than a show of it.
buzz: The cane mill runs all day and the syrup goes fast. People come back every year for the mule pull.

name: Kolomoki Mounds State Park
unique: The oldest and largest Woodland mound complex in the southeast, with Georgia's oldest great temple mound, two burial mounds and a museum built partly inside an excavated mound.
buzz: The scale of the temple mound surprises people who expect a small site. The museum is under federal review for its burial displays, so check what is open before driving.

name: Coheelee Creek Covered Bridge
unique: An 1891 covered bridge over a shoal on Coheelee Creek, the southernmost surviving covered bridge in the United States and one of the few in Georgia still standing on its original site.
buzz: Nine miles off the highway and almost always empty. The falls below the bridge are the reason people stay longer than they planned.

name: Blakely Courthouse Square
unique: A square with the 1939 city hall, the courthouse and a ring of shops that still trade, in a peanut and cotton town that has kept its grid intact.
buzz: Quiet, with a couple of good lunch counters on the square. A natural stop before Kolomoki or the covered bridge.

name: Swamp Gravy
dates: Runs in seasons, spring and autumn
unique: Georgia's official folk life play, written each year from interviews with local people and performed by neighbours at the Cotton Hall, with a cast of dozens and a live band.
buzz: The stories are the county's own and the crowd is the county's own, which is why it works. Book ahead, weekend shows sell out.

name: National Mayhaw Festival
unique: A festival for the mayhaw, the swamp hawthorn berry that makes the jelly south Georgians put on biscuits, with a cooking contest, vendors and jelly by the jar.
buzz: Forty plus years in. The jelly contest is the centre of it and the winning jars sell out early.

name: Tarrer Inn
unique: A small town inn and dining room in a historic building on the square, the place people eat before or after Swamp Gravy.
buzz: The dining room is the pre-theatre plan in Colquitt and books out on show nights. Southern plates, no rush.

name: Mark's Melon Patch
unique: A roadside farm market on Highway 82 that has sold melons, preserves, casseroles and boiled peanuts for thirty years, with a pumpkin patch and corn maze in autumn.
buzz: The casseroles and the fried pies are what people drive for. It gets shoulder to shoulder on October weekends.

name: Terrell County History Museum
unique: A log cabin museum on Stonewall Street with changing exhibits of farm equipment, vintage clothing and the records of a cotton county, run entirely by volunteers.
buzz: Small and personal, and the volunteers will talk you through the county. Free, but call first.

name: Chickasawhatchee Wildlife Management Area
unique: One of the largest wildlife management areas in the state, nineteen thousand acres of cypress swamp, gum pond and pine flatwoods with a heron rookery and a resident alligator population.
buzz: Birders come in spring for the rookery. In winter it floods and the roads close, so check conditions.

name: Fletcher Henderson House
unique: The 1888 Victorian where Fletcher Henderson grew up, the arranger whose band charts became the blueprint for swing and who put Louis Armstrong and Coleman Hawkins on the map.
buzz: A private house you look at from the street, and jazz people make the pilgrimage anyway. The claim is real and the town is proud of it.

name: Cuthbert Water Tower
unique: An 1895 water tower standing in the middle of US Highway 82, the only one in the country, because the town could not afford to move it when the road was widened.
buzz: Traffic goes around it. Locals say anyone who drinks the water either stays or comes back, and the tower is the town's whole identity in one object.

name: Center for Arts and Rehabilitative Energies
unique: An art centre spread across three buildings and thirteen acres on Shellman's main street, with a gallery that changes every two months, a studio in a barn and a lecture schedule.
buzz: A serious little arts operation in a town of a thousand. Worth checking what is hanging before you drive out.

name: King Cotton Charity Horse Show
company: Billie Lane King Cotton Charity Horse Show
unique: A charity horse show that fills Edison once a year with walking horses, saddleseat classes and a crowd that has been coming for generations.
buzz: A real competition with out of county entries, not a parade. The evening classes draw the biggest crowd.

name: Arlington Methodist Church
unique: A 1908 church on the National Register with stained glass, a corner tower and the proportions of a town that expected to grow more than it did.
buzz: One of the few listed buildings in a county with almost no preservation infrastructure. Look at it on the way through to the courthouse.

name: Calhoun County Courthouse
unique: A courthouse square in a county that fought a twenty year seat war, with Arlington taking the courthouse by a 1923 vote and Morgan keeping the town, a fight still visible in the two rival grids.
buzz: Tiny and quiet, with peanuts and cotton around it. Ask a local about the county seat fight and you will get the whole story.
